title: Any good loan broker in Sydney area (NSW)
body:
O.P.
Long story short, my loan broker freaks out with the current debt recycling arrangement and ASX shares income + franking credit.
I don't want to game the system. Neither do I want to have less borrowing capacity due to incompetent broker.
Any good loan broker in NSW who can handle debt recycling (existing) arrangements and dividends/distribution income together with franking credit correctly without freaking out?

---- replies ----
[User #7769936073 postsTerry_wwww.structuring.com.auWhirlpool Forums Addict] Debt recycling is a tax strategy that mortgage brokers cannot advise on. I am a tax solicitor that runs a mortgage broking firm, based in Sydney – can't promote it here though.
[User #9004791201 postsFinance_GuyWhirlpool Enthusiast] Nerdy Eyes writes...
Long story short, my loan broker freaks out with the current debt recycling arrangement and ASX shares income + franking credit.
What are you talking about? What do you mean by "freaking out" ? Explain the actual issue properly and I'll tell you whether your Broker is the problem or not.
[User #8540491982 postsNerdy EyesWhirlpool Enthusiast] O.P.
Terry_w writes...
Debt recycling is a tax strategy that mortgage brokers cannot advise on.
I'm not looking for an advice from the mortgage broker. I already have it in place and my tax accountant is calculating it properly.
The problem is my current mortgage broker is freaking out when she sees the investment property A has loans mortgaged with an owner occupied property and refusing to include them as negative gear-able amount.
I am a tax solicitor that runs a mortgage broking firm, based in Sydney – can't promote it here though.
You can say yes/no if I ask whether structuring.com.au is yours, no?
Finance_Guy writes...
Explain the actual issue properly and I'll tell you whether your Broker is the problem or not.
Thanks. Here it goes.
1. I have an almost paid owner occupied property. I had debt recycled from it to purchase an IP. IP loan is with bank A (50%). The rest 50% (with proper split and all) is with bank B mortgaged against my OO.
I have 2 years of tax return with proper figures aligning both loans tax deducted. Yet, she is refusing to include the loans with bank B as tax deductible loan.
2. Both my wife and I have shares and ETFs. They give dividends and distribution. Needless to say they also come with franking credits which offset against our tax bill.
Problem is broker is saying she doesn't know where to put the franking credit (I believe we need to add to our income). Actually, it seems she's never met anyone with dividend/distribution income (she's asking what they are even though she has some accounting background).
[User #92509527 postsoldandbald.lenderawww.lendera.com.auI'm new here, please be nice] Nerdy Eyes writes...
Problem is broker is saying she doesn't know where to put the franking credit (I believe we need to add to our income). Actually, it seems she's never met anyone with dividend/distribution income (she's asking what they are even though she has some accounting background).
Your broker may need to speak to their mentor or to the assigned RM at the bank for support, it should be fairly straightforward if the documents are available.
[User #6152863927 postsJamie.M Brokerwww.passgo.com.auWhirlpool Forums Addict] Nerdy Eyes writes...
The problem is my current mortgage broker is freaking out when she sees the investment property A has loans mortgaged with an owner occupied property and refusing to include them as negative gear-able amount.
That's a bit strange. If the loans are linked to an investment and you're claiming the interest – I can't see why the broker wouldn't say it's deductible.
Cheers
Jamie
